changes.detail: Every Worker-backend isolate checked its heap against `memoryLimit` every 50 ms, idle or not, so a process holding hundreds of idle isolates spent much of a core polling (300 idle isolates: 62% of a core on two cores). The check now runs every 50 ms while the isolate is busy and every second after it has been idle for a second. A host message or a sandboxed timer callback marks it busy and pulls the next check forward, so code that starts allocating after an idle spell is still stopped at the busy rate. 300 idle isolates now take 26% of a core; throughput under load is unchanged.
changes.summary: Idle Worker isolates no longer poll their heap every 50 ms

changes.detail: `IsolateOptions.requireLockdown` and `ResolveIsolatePolicyOverrides.requireLockdown` refuse an unlocked Worker-backend isolate; `ResolvedIsolatePolicy.isolate` can carry it; `Isolate.lockedDown` reports whether this isolate is locked down; `LockdownUnavailableError` (with `reason: "runtime" | "unhardened"`) is what `requireLockdown` throws.

The `ai-tool` and `plugin` policies used to require the FFI backend, so they failed wherever libJavaScriptCore was not installed. They now resolve to `backend: "auto"` with `requireLockdown: true`: FFI when the library is reachable, otherwise a Worker only when the runtime can lock it down, and `LockdownUnavailableError` on a stock Bun without libJavaScriptCore (where they threw `JscLibraryNotFoundError` before). `fallback.allowWorker` is now `true` for both. The `tenant-script` policy is unchanged and leaves `requireLockdown` unset; pass `requireLockdown: true` through `resolveIsolatePolicy` for tenants you do not trust.
changes.summary: ai-tool and plugin policies accept a locked-down Worker when FFI is unavailable

changes.detail: Code running on the Worker backend can load any module through dynamic `import()`, with no eval needed: `import("node:child_process")`, `import("node:fs")` and `import("bun:ffi")` all resolve inside a hardened isolate, on every Bun release up to and including 1.4.4. The `Bun` global also stays reachable through indirect eval and the `Function` constructor, because Bun defines it as non-configurable on Worker globals. Neither can be closed from inside the package. SECURITY.md and the README now say so, and recommend a process, container or microVM boundary around Worker-backend isolates that run code which may try to escape. No code changes.
changes.summary: Documents that the Worker backend does not contain dynamic import() or the Bun global

changes.detail: With `harden` on, the Worker backend now calls `lockdown()` from `bun:jsc` when the running Bun provides it (AbsoluteJS patched Bun 1.4.4+absolute.2 and later). It runs after the worker has loaded what it needs and before any sandboxed code, and it removes the `Bun` global (which hardening cannot delete) and `ShadowRealm`, and makes every `import()` reject. That closes the two paths by which Worker-backend code reached host authority: indirect eval or the `Function` constructor returning `Bun`, and `import("node:child_process")`, `import("node:fs")` or `import("bun:ffi")`. `isolate.lockedDown` reports whether this isolate is locked down (always `true` on the FFI backend), and the new `requireLockdown: true` option throws `LockdownUnavailableError` instead of creating an unlocked Worker-backend isolate. On stock Bun nothing changes unless `requireLockdown` is set.
changes.summary: Worker-backend isolates lock down on patched Bun, closing the Bun-global and import() escapes
